proof:
# A strict edge-midpoint consequence of the triangle cap budgets

Let a triangle have interior source y and three through-source closed halfplanes, each isolating a different strict vertex. Let q_i be their area fractions. Assume

    q_i<=c=128/279 for every i,
    sum q_i<=125/93.

Then each cap's two edge intercepts lie strictly beyond the corresponding edge midpoints when measured from its captured vertex. Equivalently, both incident edge midpoints lie strictly on the captured side of the cutting line, in the interior of its halfplane. They remain boundary points of the triangle.

## 1. Barycentric bounds

Write the barycentric coordinates of y as alpha_1,alpha_2,alpha_3. For a cap at vertex i, let u,v in (0,1) be the fractions along the edges from i to j,k where its boundary meets them. The source lies on that boundary, so

    alpha_j/u+alpha_k/v=1,       q_i=uv.

AM–GM implies q_i>=4alpha_j alpha_k.

First every alpha_i<1/2. Otherwise, relabel alpha_1>=1/2 and alpha_2>=alpha_3. For the cap at vertex 3, let u point toward vertex 1. Its fraction is alpha_2 u^2/(u-alpha_1), for alpha_1<u<=1. This decreases up to u=2alpha_1, which is at least one. Hence q_3>=alpha_2/(1-alpha_1)>=1/2, contrary to c<1/2.

Let z=max alpha_i. One of the other coordinates is at least (1-z)/2. Therefore one cap has q>=2z(1-z). Since z is in [1/3,1/2), that function is increasing. Moreover

    2(5/14)(9/14)-128/279=11/27342>0.

Thus every alpha_i<5/14.

Let m=min alpha_i, and let a,b be the other two. Since a,b<5/14 and a+b=1-m, their product is at least (5/14)(1-m-5/14): for fixed sum the product is minimized at an endpoint of the allowed interval. The opposite cap gives ab<=c/4. Consequently

    m>=9/14-7c/10=9/28+11/39060>9/28.

All source coordinates therefore lie strictly between 9/28 and 5/14.

## 2. An intercept at or before a midpoint costs too much total cap mass

Suppose the first cap has u<=1/2. Put b=alpha_2, e=alpha_3, a=1-b-e. Since b>9/28, the function e u^2/(u-b) decreases on its possible interval below one half. Hence

    q_1>=e/(2-4b),
    q_2+q_3>=4a(b+e).

Define

    F(b,e)=e/(2-4b)+4(b+e)(1-b-e).

Both b,e are in [9/28,5/14]. On that rectangle,

    partial_b F=4e/(2-4b)^2+4-8(b+e)
        >=63/25-12/7=141/175>0.

Thus F is minimized in b at 9/28. At that fixed b it is a concave quadratic in e, so its minimum is at one of the two endpoints. Their exact values are

    F(9/28,9/28)=1341/980,
    F(9/28,5/14)=269/196.

The former is smaller, and

    1341/980-125/93=2213/91140>0.

This contradicts the assumed sum bound. Every u and v must therefore be strictly greater than one half.

This is a triangle cap-incidence consequence. It does not replace a general body by a triangle or control all corner regions of an enclosing triangle. In particular, a cap that contains edge midpoints may overlap a different cap near those midpoints; no unique-signature conclusion is inferred there.
